segments.expected: Rhea Sorn sat on the tailboard of Graywater's van at eleven on Wednesday morning, the 30th of the third month, with a sheet of the Charter Board's paper on her knee and a pen in her hand, and did not write anything for a quarter of an hour.

segments.expected: "I want it." Anwen folded it once and put it in her sleeve. "I want it said I'll teach it. On the van. To the line, and to whoever Rhea puts at the far edge." She took her hand out of her sleeve again, and there was something in it, small and dark: a stick of sealing wax, red, half used, with the end of it melted and shaped by her thumb. "And this is Seven's. I've had it since the autumn. Every seal on the book and the tin. It's not mine." She held it out to Pru.

segments.expected: "I said no." Pru took the book. She held it in both capped hands against her chest, the way Loveday Hosken had held a jar. "I'd have been Ivey's catcher. I'd have been good. I'd have been the girl from Meridian on Ivey's crew who used to be Rowan's cord." She looked at Kiva. "I'm on a sheet. My own, with my name on the hem in ink. I'm going back to the Crooked Line and I'm going to find three people who've never heard of the Pit, and I'm going to catch for them, and nobody's going to say whose I was." She held the book tighter. "I'm not grateful to anybody. I'm only good. I'd like that written in the book, on the first page I write on."

segments.expected: The second called the far edge, once, before the bag. Not mine to keep.

segments.expected: Kiva got up off the cobbles. She did it one-handed, and nobody helped her, and she did not need them to.
segments.transcript: Kiva got up off the cobbles. She did it one-handed, and nobody helped her, and she did not need them to.

segments.expected: It was a long way off, out beyond the sea gate's arch and the end of the Mole, on the grey sea going dark, a low black shape with its masts against the last of the light, standing in toward Saltmere on the evening flood as the coast boat had stood in a month ago. It was too far off to see what flag it flew, or whether it flew one. It had a light on its bow.
